description: From what the person wants to the specs that do it, when no single part does it all or their wants pull against each other. Write each want as a requirement naming its route (the key of the lottery, item, grant, farm or contest it is about; its family follows from that): a draw ("pay-in" {currencies: [{token, amount}]}, "burn", "refund-as-paid", "free-entry" {grant, perPerson, spendable}, "one-approval", "one-draw", "one-token", "first-reward-no-sol"); a sale of an item ("pay-in", "fixed-price", "instant", "fair-scarce" {perPerson, list}, "one-approval"); a reward, a grant ("per-person" {claims}, "no-server", "bot-proof", "bounded" {total}, "first-reward-no-sol"; a server's voucher keys as "serverKeys" on any of them); staking, a farm ("emission-cap" {total}, "predictable", "no-lock", "whale-fair"; "perDay" and "days" on any of them); a contest ("no-owner-trust", "equal-stakes" {amount}, "refund-if-no-result"; decider keys as "serverKeys"). Pass the spec as it stands, with each route's skeleton. For each route it builds every combination of known bridges (an entry token each currency buys, crafted in the purchase; a payment held to the draw; a fixed-price listing in each currency; an allowlist; a deciding voucher server; a fixed or shared rate, minted or from a vault, with an end or a halving; a decider key), checks each, tests every requirement on it, and answers the designs best first (what the person asked for, then how it plays, then how clean, then how secure), with what each keeps (✓), keeps in part (~) and gives up (✗), a "Say" sentence for the person and what each needs from them; when none keeps them all, what has to give. Read the requirements back to the person, put the choice to them with your pick, then build the one they choose (its spec is in `designs`) and run xsolana_check on it. A spec saved before they choose is already built, a draft too: save none until they have.

example.description: A worked example by name, from xsolana_examples (coin-flip-arena, stud-farm, …).

file.description: A JSON file holding the spec, relative to the project folder (default: xsolana.json when it exists).

requirements.description: What the person wants, each a requirement the tools can test.

spec.description: An economy spec (version 2) given inline. Takes precedence over file and example.

top.description: How many designs to answer (3 by default).

name: xsolana_design
